rationale: A wins because it keeps the uncomfortable facts uncomfortable without turning them into facts it cannot prove. Its line, "Do not pitch this angle while the split is undisclosed," is exactly the adult supervision this update needs. B has usable bones, but "Klarna Won't Say How Many Customer-Service Jobs It Eliminated — But the Equivalent of 700 People Are Gone" crosses from sharp framing into an unsupported claim.
gaps_in_A: "one of the only companies publishing operational numbers" is plausible, but not supplied by the update; it needs attribution or softer wording.
The IPO angle needs the actual filing language before saying Klarna is "leading with an AI-efficiency story."
The consumer angle is smart, but "AI resolves disputes in under two minutes" slightly compresses support-chat resolution time into dispute resolution; keep that distinction clean.
gaps_in_B: "Customer-Service Jobs It Eliminated" is not grounded. The update says headcount fell about 20% and Klarna will not say roles cut versus left unfilled.
"the Equivalent of 700 People Are Gone" is worse: the update says the assistant handled the equivalent work of 700 full-time agents, not that 700 people disappeared.
"The Headcount It Cut Is the Margin It's Showing Investors" invents a direct margin claim the update does not provide.
"Every Bank and Payments Company Now Has a Public Benchmark" is overbroad trade-press hype unless B can prove banks and processors actually treat Klarna's metric as a benchmark.
